units.function: Diagnoses two Paperclip Secret providers. local_encrypted accepts a master key from environment or a resolved key file, validates three encodings, can create a random key file, checks group/other permission bits and warns when strict mode is disabled on PostgreSQL. aws_secrets_manager checks region/deployment/KMS identifiers and reports detected AWS credential-source hints without contacting AWS.
units.dependencyDirection: CLI doctor leaf -> Paperclip Secret/database configuration, environment variables, crypto randomness, runtime-path alias and direct filesystem operations. AWS diagnostics inspect process environment only; local repair embeds state-changing key generation in CheckResult. It bypasses a SecretPort/provider capability contract, approval/audit application layer and live provider health API.
units.keyDataModels: Provider enum local_encrypted|aws_secrets_manager; local master-key environment/file path; 32-byte base64, 64-hex or raw 32-character material; strictMode; AWS region/deployment/KMS identifiers and credential-source environment hints; free-form CheckResult with repair closure. No key ID/version/status/owner/purpose/tenant/rotation/expiry/attestation model is returned.
units.lifecycle: Dispatch provider -> local: prefer inline environment key, otherwise resolve file, offer a closure that mkdirs and writes a random base64 key with mode 0600, then read/decode/stat permissions; optionally downgrade pass to warn when strict mode is disabled on PostgreSQL. AWS: require non-secret identifiers, infer credential-source hints, warn only when both static access-key variables exist, otherwise pass. No encryption round-trip, vault/KMS call, rotation/revocation or consumer-resolution probe occurs.
units.testAssessment: The previously completed application:cli/__tests__/secrets assessment was reused without rereading: focused Vitest passed 8/8 and CLI TypeScript passed, proving selected inline-env migration, provider bootstrap diagnostics/routes and AWS root-credential guidance. It does not prove this check's filesystem race/symlink/owner handling, key entropy, atomic creation, real encryption/decryption, KMS alias/account/region policy, live AWS authorization, partial credentials, strict-mode enforcement, rotation or compromise recovery.
units.designRationale: Supporting workload identity/default credential chains rather than persisting AWS credentials is a strong design choice. Separating non-secret AWS deployment metadata from credentials and warning about permissive key files/disabled strict mode are useful operator safeguards. The local single-master-key convenience favors easy development over production key lifecycle and trust-domain isolation.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must manage tenant-, deployment-, Connector- and purpose-scoped Secret references across managed and local enterprise profiles, while preventing control-plane access to raw values and preserving ownership, version, rotation, authorization, usage and access evidence.
units.companyOsFit: Reimplement through a provider-neutral SecretPort plus deployment diagnostics adapter. Preserve workload identity and non-secret configuration checks, but use opaque versioned references, purpose/tenant binding, envelope/KMS-backed keys, explicit provider capability/health, rotation and revocation. Local initialization must be a separate human-authorized atomic command with allowed-root, exclusive-create, owner/mode/symlink controls and an auditable postcondition; inline long-lived master keys should be disallowed in production profiles.
units.responsibilityConflict: An arbitrary doctor repair closure can create the root encryption authority without recording the accountable human, deployment, purpose, approved path or affected Secret population. One deployment-wide master key is not enough to model separate human, Agent, Connector and tenant responsibility domains. A diagnostic pass must not imply that a principal is authorized to resolve any Secret.

units.securityFindings: Critical local-repair race: existence is checked before an unrestricted writeFileSync without an exclusive-create flag; an intervening file or symlink can be overwritten/followed. The configured path has no allowed-root, lstat/symlink, owner or parent-directory policy; mkdir is also unrestricted. chmod failure is swallowed. Permission checks inspect only mode bits after an uncaught stat and do not verify owner, regular-file type, hard links, mount policy or backup exposure. Any raw 32-character string is accepted despite unknown entropy; environment keys are long-lived process-wide values with no version/rotation checks. AWS passes on configuration presence without authenticating to STS/Secrets Manager/KMS or checking account, key state/policy and least privilege; partial static credentials are not warned. Paths, deployment ID and raw filesystem errors are exposed in messages.
